metadata.title: Consequences of the Three-Dimensional Jacobian Counterexample for Seven Neighbouring Conjectures: Implications with Their Indices and Exactly Checked Witnesses
metadata.description:
Alpöge's explicit Keller map on C^3, with a three-point fibre, refutes the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension N >= 3. Seven neighbouring conjectures are tied to it by published implications whose dimension indices decide what the map refutes. We record each implication with its theorem and index, locate all but two in a primary text, and close the implications under composition into a status table with an evidence mark per entry. Exact computations over Q and Q(i) check the map and its fibre, a homogeneous-type test, a dimension-15 homogeneous witness, a dimension-48 gradient witness, Long's rank-two Poisson map, and Long's universal pair of polynomials on SU(N) for 2 <= N <= 16 in 950 cells.

The Dixmier and Poisson conjectures fail at every index n >= 3, and the Poisson conjecture also at n = 2. The Mathieu conjecture fails on SU(N) for every N >= 2: we prove, following Long, that his pair has vanishing pure moments and positive marked moments, and the exact computation reproduces his closed forms; a homogeneous map on C^15 independently gives N >= 15. His statement for every nonabelian compact connected Lie group is read, not reproduced. The Gaussian moments conjecture fails for n >= 3, and the vanishing, Hessian and symmetric forms fail with explicit witnesses. Every check is exact, so no interval applies, and each negative control fires. The direction and index of Mathieu's implication rest on an expository rendering, and the Image implication was read only in an abstract. Dixmier at ranks 1 and 2, Poisson at index 1 and the two-variable Jacobian conjecture stay open.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/algebraic-geometry/jacobian-conjecture).
metadata.version_notes: Revision. The Mathieu row now states that the conjecture fails on SU(N) for every N >= 2, by C. D. Long's direct construction (arXiv:2609.16178): the first-column argument is proved for SU(N) in the paper and the moment identities are reproduced exactly in 950 cells for 2 <= N <= 16 (computation EXP-148). The route through the homogeneous map of dimension 15 is kept as a second route for N >= 15; the abstract, the index map, the discussion, the conclusions and the next steps are updated, and the range 3 <= N <= 14 does not carry the status of the conjecture. Adds the procedure for exact Haar moments (Algorithm 6), a table of exact values and a figure of the marked moments, and the statement of the conjecture as Long gives it; the run times of the Poisson-map check are those of its archived rerun (173.08 s).
